## 보관 원문

> # U.S. natural gas exports to grow nearly 30% by 2027 as LNG facilities ramp up
>
> - Publisher: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)
> - Published: 2026-04-16
> - Original: https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67484
> - Collected: 2026-08-19
>
> ## Relevant official text
>
> The U.S. Energy Information Administration forecasts that U.S. LNG exports will continue to increase as five LNG export projects start operations and ramp up production by the end of 2027.
>
> U.S. LNG exports are forecast to rise by 1.9 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) in 2026 to average 17.0 Bcf/d and to increase by a further 9 per cent, or 1.5 Bcf/d, in 2027.
>
> Current U.S. peak LNG export capacity is 18.3 Bcf/d. Corpus Christi Stage 3 trains 5-7 and the first two Golden Pass LNG trains are expected to add 2.0 Bcf/d during 2026. Port Arthur LNG Phase 1, Rio Grande LNG trains 1 and 2, and the final Golden Pass train are expected to begin exports in 2027.
>
> U.S. LNG exports to Europe reached 10.3 Bcf/d in 2025, up from 6.3 Bcf/d in 2024, and represented 68 per cent of U.S. LNG exports. Exports to Asia fell from 4.0 Bcf/d in 2024 to 2.5 Bcf/d in 2025, representing 16 per cent of export volumes.
>
> The forecast is an EIA projection rather than a confirmed future production result. Actual supply timing depends on project commissioning and utilisation.
